commitResults.messageTitle: Add Todo, Deadline and Event Task types
Fix input trimming and article in error messages
Save tasks to file whenever the list changes
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks are held only in memory, so the list is lost as soon as the
  program exits and the user has to retype everything on each run.

  Persist the list to ./data/harvey.txt after every command that
  changes it. Each Task subclass serialises itself through
  toFileFormat(), matching how each already renders itself through
  toString(), so adding a task type later means editing only the new
  class instead of a type check inside Storage.

  Loading is not implemented yet, so the file is written but never
  read back.

The task list is written to disk but never read back, so restarting
  Harvey still shows an empty list and the saved file is dead weight.

  Read the file in Storage.load() and start the list from it. Parsing
  cannot mirror the polymorphic toFileFormat(): there is no task yet to
  ask, so Storage reads the type letter and picks the constructor. A
  missing file means nobody has run Harvey here before, so it yields an
  empty list rather than an error, and a file that cannot be read is
  reported without stopping Harvey from starting.

  Lines that are present but malformed are not handled yet.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle damaged lines in the saved file
commitResults.messageBody:
The save file is plain text that anyone can open and edit, but every
  line was trusted. A short line crashed Harvey with an array error
  before it could start, and an unrecognised type letter quietly became
  a Todo, turning damaged data into a wrong task. Task text containing
  the field separator was also written out and then silently dropped on
  the next run.

  Check the type letter, field count, description and done flag before
  using them, and reject anything unexpected. Damaged lines are skipped
  rather than treated as fatal, so one bad line does not cost the user
  the rest of the file, and Harvey reports how many were left out so the
  loss is not mistaken for an empty file.

  Refuse the separator character when a task is created. Failing at the
  moment the user types it is clearer than accepting the task and losing
  it an hour later.
